purpose: Measure whether slower scripted approach changes the tool-contact cecum instability after the reset-contact fix.
interpretation: Reducing approach speed delays contact and changes inversion severity, but neither 6 nor 3 mm/s prevents inversion. The response is non-monotonic: the half-speed run has four inverted elements but a less negative minimum volume ratio and lower peak force, while the quarter-speed run has two inverted elements but a higher uncalibrated peak force than the 12 mm/s reference. No speed is promoted as safe or physically realistic. The default remains 12 mm/s; this parameter is exposed only to make the scripted diagnostic reproducible.
limits: One scene, one seed and one privileged scripted policy; no statistical or held-out-anatomy claim.
Force channels and tissue material parameters are not calibrated against physical instruments or specimens.
Every run completed zero appendectomy stages and failed the tissue-volume health gate.
The probe diagnoses approach-rate sensitivity; it does not establish a force-controlled policy or RL result.
privacy: Tracked report contains aggregate metrics and local ignored-run references only; source video, rendered frames, credentials and personal information remain local.
